text:
Eileen (SE): kicking off a thread for VanguardHealth POC — they want streaming responses + tool/function calls and strict JSON schema output. Main asks: sample Rust/Go SDK usage, ephemeral creds rotation, pricing delta for streaming vs batch, and SOC2/KMS requirements.
Samira (Sales): client expects ~200 rps at peak, short responses (~150 tokens). They asked if dedicated reserved capacity is needed for predictable latency.
Markus (Eng): for 200 rps with 150 tokens we usually recommend dedicated for <50ms p50; shared hosted can work but expect higher tail latency. Can we get exact SLA target?
Eileen (SE): target p95 < 250ms. Also they require function/tool callbacks to internal systems (webhooks) — security flagged ephemeral creds and least-privilege.
Raj (Security): ok for callbacks: use short-lived tokens (~15m) + broker service. We need the security questionnaire answers: does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for private deployments?
Markus (Eng): yes for Private we support customer KMS/HSM. For Hosted we encrypt at rest with our KMS; we can sign an addendum for EKM on Dedicated in enterprise contract.
Samira (Sales): pricing: can we give 2 options — hosted per-token estimate and a reserved capacity quote? Client wants to compare.
Markus (Eng): rough math: hosted token cost x* per 1M tokens. For streaming there's negligible premium per token, but sustained steady-state latency improvements come from batching; reserved: monthly commit for a GPU pool — I can generate a sample quote if you give monthly QPS target.
Eileen (SE): they may want a 1 node Dedicated pool initially for the pilot (sustained 200 rps). Can you drop a simple runbook for onboarding and SDK example?
Markus (Eng): runbook highlights: 1) Provision Dedicated pool, 2) Configure model variant + quantization profile, 3) Set routing policy to prefer regional capacity, 4) Enable KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, 5) Setup ephemeral creds.
Markus (Eng): SDK snippet (Rust) for streaming + function calls:
```rust
let client = Redwood::new_with_ephemeral("<token>");
let mut stream = client.chat_stream("gpt-redwood-4", messages).await?;
while let Some(chunk) = stream.next().await { println!("{}", chunk.text); }
```
Eileen (SE): nice — client asked about token rotation. How does ephemeral refresh work in SDK?
Markus (Eng): SDK exposes a TokenProvider trait. You implement get_token() -> refresh when TTL < 60s. We also have an IntegrationAgent (IntegrationBot) to demonstrate STS flow.
IntegrationBot: demo runbook: https://internal.redwood/poctemplates/vanguard-streaming (sample manifests + terraform snippets).
Samira (Sales): legal asks: add SOC2 + encryption answers to the questionnaire. Raj can you handle SOC2 compliance statements and KMS wording?
Raj (Security): I'll paste standard language in the questionnaire section. For callbacks we insist on IP whitelisting + mutual TLS for the webhook endpoint.
Eileen (SE): blockers: customer asked about structured JSON output validation (strict schema). Can Redwood enforce schema and fail-fast on generation drift?
Markus (Eng): we recommend output_parsers + structured response mode. Also use model rollouts + evals watch to detect drift; can auto-fallback to a safer model variant on schema violations. We can surface a webhook for schema-violation events to their telemetry.
Samira (Sales): next steps: 1) Eileen to send pilot QPS and exact SLA, 2) Markus to produce a back-of-envelope reserved quote + runbook, 3) Raj to fill security questionnaire SOC2/KMS and webhook hardening, 4) scheduling a 30m tech kickoff with Vanguard (prob next Tue).
Eileen (SE): assigned — will send QPS + legal contact by EOD. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Markus (Eng): I'll produce the quote and the Dedicated node checklist by tomorrow AM.
Raj (Security): will draft SOC2/KMS answers and webhook mTLS/IP whitelist guidance.
Samira (Sales): ping me when draft quote is ready, I'll include in the pricing comparison.
Eileen (SE): tagging for visibility — @Samira @Markus @Raj — will update thread when I have the QPS doc.
